transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve started to feel like I’m just not good enough at anything anymore, no matter how hard I try. It just feels like I'm constantly falling short, and my doctor thought it would be best for me to come speak with you.
How long have you been feeling this way, is it something that started recently or has it been going on for a while?

It's actually been going on continuously for a little over two years now. It started around the time my husband and I began fertility treatments, and this heavy, low mood just hasn't really lifted since then.
Have you noticed any decrease in interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy before these feelings of inadequacy started?

Yes, I've really lost interest in things I used to love. I used to paint, but now it's just a distraction to keep my mind busy, and I've withdrawn from shared activities with my husband. I've also stopped going to our Sunday family dinners and turn down friends' invitations because I just don't have the emotional energy or excitement for them anymore.
Have you experienced any significant weight changes or alterations in your appetite over the past two years, and if so, how would you describe them?
I haven't really noticed any major changes in my appetite or my weight over the last couple of years. That hasn't really been a prominent issue for me amidst everything else.

Have you experienced any periods over the past two years where your mood and interest in activities significantly improved for a while before returning to how you've been feeling, or has it been a consistent low mood throughout?

No, there haven't really been any periods where it got better. It has been a consistent, low-grade sadness dragging me down pretty much continuously since we started the fertility treatments two years ago. Even when something good happens, that heavy feeling never really lifts.

Can you tell me if there have been any times during these two years where you felt really down and hopeless for a shorter period, like a couple of weeks, followed by a return to your baseline low mood, or has it been one long, continuous stretch of feeling this way?

It has definitely been one long, continuous stretch of feeling this way. My heavy, low mood has just been a constant, unchanging baseline for the past two years, without any distinct periods where it got significantly worse for a few weeks and then recovered back to normal.

You've mentioned a continuous low mood for two years without significant improvements or worsening episodes, can you help me understand if there have been any times when your low mood or lack of interest in activities became so severe that you had trouble functioning in your daily life, such as going to work or taking care of yourself?

I still force myself to go to work and get my teaching duties done, but I completely collapse as soon as I get home. Because of that, I've had to let my husband handle almost all of the household chores. I've also been avoiding family dinners and friends' invitations because I just don't have the physical or emotional energy to be present anymore.
Do you often feel guilty or worthless about not being able to achieve your goals or live up to your expectations, and if so, how does that impact your daily life?

Yes, I constantly feel like I'm failing, and there's this running commentary in my head telling me I’m a bad wife for not being able to get pregnant and a mediocre teacher who is letting her students down. It has impacted my life so much that I've started turning down family dinners, avoiding friends, and leaving almost all the household chores to my husband because I just don't have the energy to be present anymore.
Can you describe how your feelings of guilt, worthlessness, and low self-esteem have affected your ability to make decisions or take care of yourself on a daily basis?

The constant negative commentary in my head telling me I'm a bad wife and a mediocre teacher leaves me feeling completely drained. On a daily basis, this lack of energy makes it so hard to take care of basic chores that I just collapse on the couch after work and rely on my husband to handle everything. I've also been avoiding decisions like responding to social invitations or going to family dinners because I just don't have the emotional bandwidth to deal with them.
Have you ever experienced any thoughts or beliefs that seem unreal or heard voices that others cannot hear during these two years of feeling low and inadequate?
No, I have never experienced anything like that. I've never heard any unusual voices, seen things that weren't there, or had beliefs that felt unreal.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'collapse' when you get home from work, and how that affects your ability to engage in any activities or self-care in the evenings?

When I say "collapse," I mean I lie on the couch with absolutely no energy left after forcing myself to stay upbeat for my students all day. Even basic tasks like loading the dishwasher feel like too much effort, so I just let my husband handle all the household chores. I simply don't have the physical or emotional energy to do anything in the evenings.

You've described a continuous low mood for two years without distinct episodes of worsening, but can you clarify if there have been any subtle variations in the intensity of your symptoms over time, even if they didn't significantly impact your daily functioning?

It really is a remarkably constant, flat sadness, almost like a steady gray fog that never truly lifts even when good things happen. While there aren't any "better" days, the heaviness can feel a bit more intense or raw at certain times, like right after a failed fertility cycle or around those Sunday family dinners. Otherwise, it has just been a continuous, draining baseline for the last two years.

You've described a continuous low mood without distinct episodes of worsening, but can you confirm if there have been any periods, even brief, where you felt nearly normal or significantly better, which would help differentiate between a persistent low-grade depression and episodes of more severe depression?

No, there haven't been any periods where I felt normal or even slightly better. This heavy, low-grade sadness has been completely constant and continuous for the past two years without any breaks or relief. Even when something good happens, that gray feeling never really lifts.

Can you confirm if you have experienced any distinct episodes of depression that lasted for at least two weeks, with at least five symptoms of depression, including either depressed mood or loss of interest, and if these episodes were interspersed with periods where your mood and functioning were significantly better?

No, I haven't had distinct, separate episodes with periods of feeling significantly better in between. This heavy, low mood has just been a constant, continuous presence for the last two years without any real breaks or periods of normal functioning.

To clarify, you're saying that over the past two years, you haven't had any periods that lasted at least two weeks where your symptoms were significantly worse, with more intense feelings of sadness, loss of interest, or other symptoms of depression, followed by periods where you felt somewhat better, but instead, it's been a constant low-grade feeling?

Yes, that's exactly right. I haven't had any distinct, severe episodes that eventually lifted; it has just been a continuous, heavy gray feeling dragging me down for the past two years. While some days are naturally a bit harder than others, it's always been this steady, constant low-grade sadness without any breaks where I felt normal or better.
